title: When you are worse: make it hard, and decide with a reason
outcomes: Lists the resources a worse position can have: a repeated check, a stalemate trick, a fortress, a move that sets a problem
Counts the opponent's winning replies to pick the move that sets the most problems among moves that all lose
Tests a swindle against the opponent's best reply before relying on it
Writes a play-on or resign decision with a reason and knows it is a judgement

steps.text: **Worse is not lost.** When you are behind, aim for the line that is hardest for the opponent, not the slowest loss. Your resources: a repeated check (a perpetual), a stalemate trick, a fortress, a move that sets a problem. Each has exact conditions and each can be tested against the opponent's best reply. Whether to give up the game is a different question: no source gives evidence, so we call it a judgement.

**Exact conditions.** A perpetual needs a safe check at every turn: count the king's squares. A stalemate trick needs two things: the stronger side has no better reply than taking the offered piece, and after that capture the weaker side has no legal move at all. A fortress needs its key squares held. A trap is worth setting only if the right reply costs you nothing (our rule of thumb).

steps.title: A fortress, and one change
steps.prompt: In the first position the defender holds a fortress. In the second, one thing is different. Predict the result each time, then check.

steps.text: No labels now. In each position the side to move is behind in material. Name the drawing resource it offers, or say there is none. Then check it against the opponent's best reply. The perpetual and the stalemate trick are taught in *Perpetual check: the draw you can force* and *Stalemate as a rescue*. The next two exercises are silent.
**Resign or play on?** Our working hypothesis, not a fact: play on while a resource exists and the game still teaches you something; resign when none is left.

steps.prompt: Choose a worse position from one of your own games. Write what you checked and what you decided. Keep a short log of ten such positions on paper or in your notes (the app does not track this yet), with the result, so that the working rule can be tested on you.
